sup.stockout.subject: Urgent: can you deliver {item:item} quickly?
sup.stockout.body:
Dear {supplier} team,

Our stock of {item:item} is {onhand:n0} {unit:unit}, enough for about {lasts:dur}, and demand is rising. Please tell us the earliest delivery date and how much you can deliver within {lead:n0} days, ideally with fast shipping.

Best regards,
Procurement
sup.delay.subject: Urgent: order {po} of {item:item} is late
sup.delay.body:
Dear {supplier} team,

Our order {po} for {qty:n0} {unit:unit} of {item:item}, placed on {order_date:date}, is now late and expected on {eta:date}. We have only {onhand:n0} {unit:unit} left, enough for about {lasts:dur}, and production would stop in about {hours:dur}.

Please (1) confirm a firm delivery date and (2) send the first available quantity right away.
sup.delay.alt:
As a stopgap we could also take {alt:item}. Please tell us if it is available and how fast.

Best regards,
Procurement
sup.safety.subject: Please prioritise our order of {item:item}
sup.safety.body:
Dear {supplier} team,

Our stock of {item:item} is {onhand:n0} {unit:unit}, below the {ss:n0} we want to keep. Please prioritise our next order and confirm the delivery date.

Best regards,
Procurement

help.title: Help
help.tour_text: A short tour of the screen in 5 steps.
guide.title: Welcome to SmartStock
guide.s1.b: The clock at the top shows the simulated date and hour. Press Start and the warehouse works hour by hour: items are used, deliveries arrive, batches expire.
guide.s2.b: “1 hour = 5 seconds” is the speed. Open Speed to make it faster or slower. You can pause at any time. The clock pauses by itself when something critical happens.
guide.s3.b: “Needs your decision” lists what the system suggests: orders, messages to suppliers, storage requests. Each card says why, what happens if you approve, and what happens if you do nothing.
guide.s4.b: Every item has a status with an icon: Critical, Running low, OK, Too much, Expiring soon. “Lasts” tells you how long the stock will last at the current use.
guide.s5.b: After you approve or reject, an Undo button appears for a few seconds. “After your decisions” shows what each decision led to. The ? button brings back this tour, the demo and the glossary.
demo.intro: Follow these steps to see the whole story in about two minutes.
demo.s1: Look at the top: it is 5 October, midnight. Under “What is at risk” you see which items may run out.
demo.s2: Press Start. Movements appear under “What happened recently”. Try Speed → 1 s.
demo.s3: When frozen shrimp shells run out, the clock pauses and says why. Read the red message.
demo.s4: In “Needs your decision”, open the order for that item and press the green button to approve it.
demo.s5: Reject another order and keep running: see how the shortage grows because nothing was ordered.
demo.s6: Use More → Jump to next day to see the approved delivery arrive at its hour.
demo.s7: Open “Storage space”, approve a customer request, and watch the free space change when the rental starts.
demo.s8: Open “After your decisions” to read, in plain sentences, what each of your choices led to.
gl.lasts.def: How long the stock on hand lasts if we keep using it at the recent rate.
gl.order_point.def: The stock level at which a new order should be placed so it arrives before we run out.
gl.lead.def: The number of days a supplier needs to deliver after we order.
gl.safety.def: The minimum amount we want to always have on hand, in case demand or delivery surprises us.
gl.overstock.def: More stock than we will use for many weeks. The system does not order more of it.
gl.expiring.def: A batch whose expiry date is close and which we may not use in time.
gl.lot.def: A quantity of an item received together, with one expiry date.
gl.lease.def: Space we rent out to another company for a number of months.
gl.rentable.def: Space nobody is using, which is not kept for our own growth and is allowed to be rented out.
gl.buffer.def: Space we deliberately keep empty for our own future stock.
gl.season.def: How much higher demand is expected in the busy months, for example ×1.8 means 80% more.
gl.spike.def: Use that is more than double what it normally was in the previous weeks.
gl.critical_level.def: How essential an item is for production. A is essential, B important, C can wait.
gl.forecast.def: Our estimate of how much will be used in the coming weeks, based on recent use and the season.
